challenges.name: Inspect the Market
challenges.idea: the server sends your browser the whole page, comments and all; the inspector shows it
challenges.description: A little shop. The browser on the left is already pointed at it. Use the inspector on the right to read what the server actually sent back.
hints: Click the first row in the Network panel (the right side), then open its Response tab: that is what the server sent.
Web pages often carry notes the author left in HTML comments: <!-- like this -->. The browser does not draw them, but they were still sent to you.

headers.X-Fanum-Tax: one grape per bag, collected at the door

routes.body:

today's deals

challenges.name: Wrong Turn
challenges.idea: the browser follows a redirect and never shows the first reply; the inspector kept a copy of it
challenges.description: A diner with a side door. Click the link and you arrive somewhere else. The interesting part is the reply you were hurried past.
hints: Click the link in the browser on the left, then look at the inspector: there are new rows, and one of them is the side-door row with Status 302.
Click the 302 row and open its Response tab. The browser followed the redirect and never showed you that first reply, but the inspector saved it.

routes.body:
Detour Diner

challenges.name: Front Desk
challenges.idea: a check that runs in your browser is written in the page the server sent you
challenges.description: A hotel front desk. The sign-in checks your passphrase right there in the page. Read what the page actually sent you.
hints: Click the first row (the sign-in page) in the Network panel and open its Response tab: there is a <script> in there.
The script compares what you type to one fixed passphrase. Type that passphrase into the passphrase box and sign in.

routes.body:

challenges.name: Price Check
challenges.idea: the shop puts every price in the order form your browser sends; the server adds up whatever numbers arrive
challenges.description: Loot Lane, an online store. Your shopping list costs way more than your wallet holds. Check out anyway.
hints: Type the quantities from the shopping list, press Add to cart, then Place order. Your wallet says no. Click the new order row in the Network panel and open its Payload tab: look at everything your browser sent besides the quantities.

Every price rides along in the order your browser sends, and the shop just adds them up. Press Edit and Resend, change the prices in the Body box to tiny numbers (keep the quantities the same) and press Send.

challenges.name: Members Only
challenges.idea: the cookie your browser sends on every request is yours to change
challenges.description: A members club. You are let in as a guest. The lounge is for members only. See if the inspector can get you in.
hints: Click the first row in the Network panel and read Response Headers in its Headers tab: the server set a cookie that says role=guest. Your browser now sends that cookie on every request.
Click the members lounge link, then click the new lounge row, press Edit and Resend, change the Cookie line in the Headers box so role is admin, then press Send.

challenges.name: Fortune Cookies
challenges.idea: a cookie can hold a number you step through; one value is special
challenges.description: A fortune cookie stand. Every cookie is numbered and your browser remembers which one you are on. There are 7 fortunes.
hints: Click the first row and read Response Headers in its Headers tab: the server set a cookie called fortune. Then click the open your cookie link, click the new crack row, press Edit and Resend, and find that cookie in the Headers box.
Change the number in the fortune cookie and press Send. There are 7 fortunes, numbered 0 to 6. One of them is special.

challenges.name: Staff Door
challenges.idea: your browser also sends headers, and you can set those to anything
challenges.description: A company webmail. The admin inbox only opens for the company's own browser. You are not using the company's browser... or are you?
hints: Click the first row in the Network panel and open its Response tab. The developers left a note behind in there, in an HTML comment the browser never draws: <!-- like this -->.
Click the admin inbox link, then click the inbox row, press Edit and Resend, and change the User-Agent line in the Headers box to the value from that note, then press Send.

challenges.name: Knock Differently
challenges.idea: HTTP methods: the server refuses one method with a status and an Allow header naming the right one
challenges.description: A club with a very particular doorman. Ask the wrong way and he tells you exactly how to ask.
hints: Click the vault link, then click the vault row (it is red) and read its Headers tab: the Status Code and an Allow header.
The Allow header names the method the doorman accepts. Press Edit and Resend, change the method dropdown to that method and press Send, then read Response Headers on the new row.

routes.body:

challenges.name: Wrong Number
challenges.idea: changing an id in the URL shows a different record; the server never checks who is asking
challenges.description: A shop keeps every receipt online. Yours is number 1001. The manager's is not your business, but the server will hand it to anyone.
hints: Open your receipt with the link, then click the receipt row in the Network panel and look at the Request URL: it ends in id=1001.
Press Edit and Resend, change the id in the URL to the manager's number (it was on the home page) and press Send. The server never checks whose receipt you asked for.

challenges.name: Back Office
challenges.idea: a page viewer loads files by name from one folder; ../ climbs out to a file it never meant to serve
challenges.description: A café lets you read its pages by name. The pages live in the public folder. The kitchen keeps something better upstairs.
hints: Open the menu link, then click the view row in the Network panel. Its URL asks for a page by name (Edit and Resend lets you change it). Ask for a page that is not there and read the error: it shows the exact path the server looked in.
The error shows you are inside /public. Use ../ (the same as cd .. in the terminal) to climb out of /public, then go into the secret folder. The file is called flag.txt.

routes.body:
